fifo_lifo.title: Stack order instead of queue order
fifo_lifo.explain: A queue serves the vertex that has waited longest (first in, first out). Taking the newest vertex first is how a stack works, and it turns BFS into a different search.
fifo_lifo.label: Watch the queue (Module 3, 02)

wrong_layer.title: Skipping ahead a level
wrong_layer.explain: BFS finishes every vertex 1 edge away before any vertex 2 edges away. A vertex further out can't come before a closer one.
wrong_layer.label: Watch the ripples (Module 3, 01)

mark_on_serve.title: Marking a vertex too late
mark_on_serve.explain: A vertex is marked found the moment it joins the queue. If marking waited until it's served, two neighbours could both add it.
mark_on_serve.label: See D join twice (Module 3, 03)

duplicate.title: Adding a vertex twice
duplicate.explain: Once a vertex is found, it never joins the queue again, whether it's waiting or already served.
duplicate.label: See the bug and the fix (Module 3, 03)

parent_reversed.title: Parent and child swapped
parent_reversed.explain: A vertex's parent is the vertex that found it, one edge closer to the start. Follow parents back towards the start, never away from it.
parent_reversed.label: Watch the route retraced (Module 4, 03)

unreachable.title: Expecting to reach every vertex
unreachable.explain: BFS only travels along edges. A vertex with no chain of edges from the start is never found, however long you search.
unreachable.label: Vertices you can't reach (Module 4, 05)

count_places_not_edges.title: Counting vertices instead of edges
count_places_not_edges.explain: A route's length is the number of edges crossed. A, C, E has 3 vertices but 2 edges.
count_places_not_edges.label: Count edges (Module 4, 06)

length_is_cost.title: Treating drawn length as cost
length_is_cost.explain: In an unweighted graph every edge counts as one step, however long it's drawn.
length_is_cost.label: Edges cost the same (Module 2, 03)

one_way_edge.title: Storing an edge one way only
one_way_edge.explain: An undirected edge goes in both vertices' lists. Missing one makes it a one-way edge.
one_way_edge.label: Edges go both ways (Module 2, 03)
